turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I would be happy to call, ma'am, but I am afraid I don't know where Estella is, or what she looks like, or anything about her, so I might make a mistake.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy! You should know the layout of my house, I pay you to be a companion to Estella, not to be a clumsy, ignorant child. Go to the top of the stairs and call her.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will go to the top of the stairs and call Estella, and you will not return until she has come to you. Do not disappoint me, boy.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella will be delighted to see you, I daresay, so do not keep her waiting.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Do not dawdle, boy, or I shall have to tell you what it means to keep me waiting.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, I don't rightly know how to call Estella, I've never seen her before, and I don't want to make a mistake.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You dare to question my instructions? I have told you to call Estella, and I expect you to obey me without hesitation. Now, boy, go to the top of the stairs and do as you are told!

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will address her by her name, Estella, and say 'Estella, Miss Havisham summons you', in a voice that carries to the top of the stairs. Do not mumble or whisper, boy.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, I daresay, is taking a long time to arrive. Do not waste another moment, boy, and go to find her!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, I've gone to the top of the stairs and called out as you said, but there's been no answer.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, I don't think she's in her room, and I'm not sure what to do next.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, I've looked everywhere and I still can't find Estella. Should I go out into the garden and see if she's there?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, I've looked everywhere and I still can't find Estella. I'm worried that she might be...ah...elsewhere, and I don't know what to do next.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy! You've had ample time to find Estella, and I will not be made a mockery of by your incompetence. Go out into the garden at once and fetch her back to me!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, I'm not sure I should go out into the garden alone, especially if Estella is...ah...elsewhere. I'm worried it might not be safe for me.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, you will not be safe? Ha! You will do as you are told, or you will leave my estate at once. I will not be disobeyed!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I-I'm sorry, ma'am, but I don't think I can leave your estate without your permission. I'm just a poor boy from the village, and I don't have anywhere else to go.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You dare to question my authority? I am your benefactress, and I will not be disobeyed. You will do as I say, or suffer the consequences!

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You have been instructed to address me as 'ma'am', but you seem to have forgotten. I will not be reminded of your station by your impertinence. Now, I ask you again, go and fetch Estella at once!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I-I'll try, ma'am, but could you please tell me what I'm supposed to do with Estella if she comes? I don't want to get into trouble, and I don't know what I'm expected to do.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
